method: Reviewed ATT&CK ICS Remote Services coverage against CME controls that govern remote-service authentication, authorization, and network segmentation for OT and adjacent systems. Accepted only controls that concretely enforce the ATT&CK ICS mitigations listed for T0886.

candidates_considered.rationale: Identity-aware gateways concretely implement access management for remote service entry points.
Host-level filtering can block unauthorized remote service sources and protocols.
Segmentation limits movement between business, management, and OT network zones.
Multi-factor authentication raises the bar for remote human access to ICS-adjacent services.
Kerberos/GSSAPI provides concrete mutual authentication for supported remote service workflows.
Encrypted transport alone does not provide the ATT&CK ICS access-control guarantees needed to mitigate remote service abuse.

evidence: CME covers the ATT&CK ICS remote-service mitigation theme through controls for access management, traffic filtering, segmentation, and strong authentication.
Rejected entries were excluded when they protected confidentiality in transit but did not directly constrain remote service access or authorization.
